authors: L.V. Avdeev, G.A. Chochia, A.A. Vladimirov
title: On the scope of supersymmetric dimensional regularization
claim: Superfield DRED is internally inconsistent; a component-field reformulation removes the ambiguity, but that version violates the supersymmetric Ward identities at higher loop orders. For several models the authors determine the range (domain) in which the method is still valid; this range covers the calculations done up to then.
loop_order: earliest possible violation of the propagator SUSY Ward identity of pure N=1 SYM: 4 loops (per S2.09); identity holds to 3 loops (per S2.10)
theory: pure N=1 SYM in Wess-Zumino gauge (the case reconstructed in S2.09 Sec. 4); 'several models' in the abstract
scheme: Component DRED (ACV formulation), anticommuting gamma5, minimal subtraction.
symmetry_argument: Quantum-action-principle argument: the SUSY variation of the DRED action is delta L_S = (g/2) f^{abc} epsbar gamma^mu lambda^a lambda^b gamma_mu lambda^c (S2.09 eq. 29), which vanishes in d=4 only by Fierz rearrangement. Inserted into a diagram it contributes through Delta = Tr(A gamma^mu B gamma_mu) + Tr(A gamma^mu)Tr(B gamma_mu) - (-1)^k Tr(A gamma^mu B^R gamma_mu) (S2.09 eq. 36); for five gamma matrices in A and in B this is 48 times the antisymmetrised five-index Kronecker delta (S2.09 eqs. 37-38), with trace 48 d(d-1)(d-2)(d-3)(d-4), zero only for integer d <= 4. Enough gamma matrices to make this survive in the propagator Ward identity need at least four loops.

proved: (Within their assumptions) the Fierz-violating insertion cannot spoil the SUSY propagator Ward identity of pure SYM below four loops.
assumed: The quantum action principle for component DRED (only argued much later, S2.10 Sec. 3).

evidence: S2.09 hep-ph/9707278 Sec. 4, eqs. (27)-(38): reconstruction of the argument; 'at least four loops' statement.
S2.10 hep-ph/0503129 Sec. 4.1: ACV assumed the QAP and argued the propagator identity holds to three loops; source of the breaking term Delta_gauge (eq. 35b of S2.10).
red_flags: No explicit four-loop computation of the breaking; the counting argument itself is not reproduced in either secondary source.
The abstract's 'domains of validity' could not be checked against the original text.
cross_checks: S2.05_Avdeev1982 (claimed explicit 3-loop breaking of coupling relations, later disputed)
source_access: abstract only (INSPIRE) + secondary: hep-ph/9707278 Sec. 4 and hep-ph/0503129 Sec. 4.1
notes: The four-loop statement concerns the propagator Ward identity of pure SYM; it is not a statement about beta functions.
